subject: Quantization trade study & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwave.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 14:15:00 -0800
Subject: Quantization trade study & evaluation plan

Thanks for the call today — good to meet the FinWave team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear eval plan: 

Summary / ask: FinWave wants to serve an extraction/classification assistant with sub-200ms P95 latency and < $0.015 per 1k token unit cost target. You're sensitive to quality regressions on financial-fact extraction.

Recommended models to evaluate:
- meta-llama/Llama-3-70b (FP16 baseline) — best quality baseline for your prompts
- Llama-3-70b AWQ/GPTQ 4/8-bit variants — likely best latency/cost tradeoffs
- Falcon-40B-instruct (quantized) — lower cost option, check hallucination risk

Quantization/throughput trade study (high level):
- AWQ: good quality retention at 4-bit in many benchmarks, strong throughput wins on A100/RTX8000 equivalents; may require AWQ-specific kernels.
- GPTQ: mature tooling, predictable 4/8-bit behavior, often slightly higher quality vs aggressive AWQ 4-bit on extraction tasks.
- FP8 (mixed): lower memory with potential perf uplift on latest HW (H100/OL-optimized stacks) but tighter numerical stability; recommended only if you plan to run on FP8-capable infra.

Proposed eval plan (what we'll run for you):
1) Run a 24-48h automated eval across your prompt set: FP16 baseline, GPTQ-8, GPTQ-4, AWQ-4 (where available), and FP8 where infra allows.
2) Metrics: extraction F1, instruction-following accuracy, P95 latency, median latency, token cost estimate, and a manual spot-check for regression examples.
3) Deliverables: CSV of model outputs + diff flags, per-model benchmarking sheet, and a short recommendation with deployment config (batching, KV cache settings, quantization choice).

Attachments: I attached the prompt set we captured (finwave_eval_prompt_set_v1.json) and a short tradeoffs deck.

Next steps / asks from you:
- Confirm the prompt set and any additional eval scenarios to include (e.g., long-context docs, multi-turn flows).
- Confirm target infra for the FP8 experiments (do you have H100/Cloud instances?).
- Approve a 2-hour pilot run next Wednesday so we can start the automated baseline generation.

If that looks good I can get Neha (SE) to schedule the run and share the expected QPS/latency numbers per model.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: finwave_eval_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt set, 78 prompts), quant_tradeoffs_awq_gptq_fp8.pdf (trade study summary)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwave.com>

Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quantization trade study & evaluation plan

Thanks Marissa — that recap captures it. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- Primary concern: extraction accuracy for ticker/amount/entity fields. Even small drops in precision are a blocker.
- Infra: we have a mix — GCP A2s (A100) in prod, and access to H100 on a limited basis for batch experiments.
- Cost target is aspirational; we'd accept slightly higher if latency/quality is met.

We'd like Neha to focus on: 1) a small set of 20 high-priority prompts that historically surface the most regressions, and 2) a QPS profile: expect ~150 QPS peak for a 10k daily active user pattern (bursty).

Can you confirm expected P95 for GPTQ-8 and AWQ-4 vs FP16 on A100? If you can share rough numbers that'd help our procurement planning. Also loop in our infra lead (I'll introduce separately) for the FP8 runs.

—Alex
Director of AI, FinWave
alex.johnson@finwave.com

Hi Alex — added Neha here (SE) and thanks for the details. We've prepared a short trade-study and perf estimate attached. Key calls: 

1) Expected P95 latencies on A100 (single-request, small context ~80 tokens, conservative batching):
- FP16 (Llama-3-70b): ~180-240ms P95
- GPTQ-8 (Llama-3-70b): ~120-160ms P95 (~25-35% improvement vs FP16)
- AWQ-4 (Llama-3-70b): ~70-110ms P95 (~55-70% improvement vs FP16) — note: AWQ requires specific kernel support; numbers assume AWQ-optimized runtime.
- FP8 (where supported): ~60-90ms P95 but only if run on FP8-optimized instances and kernels.

2) Quality expectations on your extraction prompts (empirical):
- GPTQ-8: minimal regression on extraction F1 (<1-2% drop vs FP16) in our internal spot checks.
- AWQ-4: good for many QA/summary tasks but can show edge-case extraction drops (2-6% F1) depending on tokenization and prompt phrasing.
- FP8: quality similar to FP16 in many flows but higher variance; recommended only for experiments on controlled infra.

3) Proposed pilot: we will run the 20-priority prompt set you requested plus a 3k prompt randomized sample overnight. Deliverables: per-prompt outputs, diff flags, and a short deck highlighting any regressions and suggested mitigations (re-prompting, calibration, or fallback to GPTQ-8 for flagged prompts).

Attached: quant_tradeoffs_awq_gptq_fp8.pdf (trade study) and finwave_sample_outputs.csv (sample outputs + diffs).

I can schedule a 30-minute sync to review the initial results next Monday. Would 10am PT work?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
